questions.question: You select a model in the Microsoft Foundry model catalog. What must you do before you can chat with the model in the chat playground?

options.text: Create a deployment of the model
options.why: Correct. The playground and applications call a deployment, not the catalog entry.
Fine-tuning is optional and not required to chat with a model.
Serverless deployments do not require you to create virtual machines.
The playground lets you chat without writing code.

questions.explanation: A model must be deployed to your Foundry resource before the playground or an application can send it requests.

questions.scenario: You deploy gpt-4.1-mini and set the deployment name to support-bot. A developer writes code that calls the deployment.
questions.question: Which value should the developer pass as the model parameter?

options.why: This is the catalog model name. Code must use the deployment name.
Correct. Requests reference the deployment name.
The resource name is part of the endpoint, not the model parameter.
The project ID does not identify the deployment.

questions.explanation: Applications pass the deployment name as the model parameter.

questions.question: While testing in the chat playground, you need the model to give more focused and repeatable answers. Which parameter change should you make?

options.why: A higher temperature makes answers more varied.
Correct. A lower temperature makes output more deterministic.
Presence penalty encourages new topics. It does not make answers more repeatable.

options.text: Reduce the number of past messages included
options.why: This changes how much history is sent, not how random the answer is.

questions.explanation: Lower temperature values produce more focused and consistent responses.

questions.question: Which TWO statements about the Global Standard deployment type are true?

options.why: Correct. Global Standard is a pay-per-token deployment type.

options.text: Requests can be processed in any Azure region
options.why: Correct. Global deployments route requests across Azure's global infrastructure.

options.text: It requires you to purchase provisioned throughput units
options.why: Provisioned throughput units apply to provisioned deployment types.

options.text: It guarantees that processing stays inside the EU data zone
options.why: Data Zone Standard provides data zone processing, not Global Standard.

questions.explanation: Global Standard is the default starting point: pay per token, with requests that can be processed in any region. Data at rest stays in the resource's geography.

questions.question: You have tuned a system message and parameters in the chat playground. You need sample code that calls the deployment with the same settings. What should you use?

options.text: The View code option in the playground
options.why: Correct. View code shows sample code with the endpoint, deployment name and current settings.

options.text: The model card in the catalog
options.why: Model cards describe the model. They do not contain your playground settings.
The Activity log records management operations, not sample code.
Evaluations measure response quality and safety; they do not generate client code.

questions.explanation: View code in the playground generates sample code that matches the current deployment, system message and parameters.
